decisionQuestion: What exact V1C privileged architecture should MIHVER adopt for the Authorization Ledger, human R3 AuthorizationGrant administration, trusted Council/evidence import boundary, and persistent global stopEpoch register, while preserving strict privilege separation and guaranteeing zero execution-effect consumers? This is a NEW candidate (decision-4); the prior candidate (decisionHash sha256:540531...b6e9f3) was REJECTED by seat-openai and is permanently closed -- do not resubmit it, cosmetically rename it, or reuse its architecture unless materially revised.
evidence: MANDATORY: your candidate MUST NOT claim 'zero execution consumers' while also describing any downstream execution-tier consumption flow. ALLOW_ONCE/checkAndConsume may exist as privileged state only; no production component may consume it to perform an effect in V1C. A future V1D handoff must be described only as a dormant interface requiring a separate ADR.

MANDATORY: define stopEpoch's exact privileged owner, serialized/transactional increment mechanism, restart persistence, corruption/ambiguity handling, stale-epoch rejection, and why no normal ADMIN/CLIENT API can decrement or reset it.

MANDATORY: define mechanically enforceable privilege separation: process identity, OS user/group, ADMIN vs CLIENT capability split, filesystem ownership, IPC permissions, trusted-registry mutation authority, evidence import authority, grant issuance authority, stopEpoch mutation authority. 'Logically separate' alone is insufficient.

Baseline to evaluate: a dedicated privileged Authorization Ledger service, structurally separate from Publication Broker, with its own OS identity, separate ADMIN and CLIENT Unix-domain sockets with filesystem permissions and OS peer-credential checks, SQLite/WAL transactional storage, a trusted CouncilEpochRegistry, canonical privileged-validated evidence import (never trusting caller-supplied hash-shaped artifacts by default), persistent monotonic stopEpoch, exact-bound AuthorizationGrant records, a consume-once ledger, and transactional audit -- with ZERO production consumer of checkAndConsume/ALLOW_ONCE at V1C exit. You may select a different design only if you explain why it is materially safer or simpler for MIHVER's actual local single-machine threat model.

Do NOT select HSM/TPM/enclave/hypervisor isolation/M-of-N human ceremony/Merkle-SMT state/air-gap/distributed consensus unless you name a concrete threat that simpler local OS-level privilege separation (dedicated OS user, Unix socket peer-credential checks, SQLite WAL, filesystem permissions) does not adequately mitigate. Prefer least privilege, deterministic correctness, crash safety, auditability, small attack surface, and implementability over mechanisms that merely sound stronger.

Claude and Codex must never hold ADMIN capability or credentials, must never be able to create an AuthorizationGrant, alter the trusted Council registry, or change stopEpoch, under any circumstance in your design.
Keep your JSON payload concise and concrete enough that a fresh implementation team could implement it without reopening basic trust-boundary decisions, but do not include chain-of-thought.
